- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive or neutral (especially after recent spikes).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low, particularly in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is above 70–75% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.20 within 3 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day for next 5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is rising; cap forecast at 10% above recent 10-day high.
